title: To Stew Potatoes
description: Prepared with potatoes, onion, and butter.
steps: Peel 4 or 5 large potatoes, cut them in square pieces.
Chop an onion very fine, put it in a saucepan with {{source-2}}, let it fry.

Pour over 1/2 pint of cold milk.
Set them on to cook, let them simmer till done, be careful the potatoes do not break.
When done the sauce will look like cream.
Turn them into a vegetable dish and sprinkle over chopped parsley; send up very hot.

title: To Stew Quinces
description: Prepared with quinces, rind, and vinegar.
steps: Peel the quinces, quarter and core them

When nearly done add 2 tablespoonfuls of vinegar
Finish them off by quick boiling

title: To Stew Spinach with Eggs
description: Prepared with spinach, eggs, and onion.

ingredients.name: 2 spoonfuls of oil or 2 ounces of butter
ingredients.sourceText: 2 spoonfuls of oil or 2 ounces of butter

steps: Wash and pick the spinach well, pass it through several waters, put it to drain.
Put it in a saucepan with some salt, no water, put it at the side to boil, spinach gives a great deal of water.
When done put it in a colander to drain, then chop it very fine on a board.
Chop very fine in a saucepan an onion, fry it with 2 spoonfuls of oil, or 2 ounces of butter.
Put a teacup of boiling water.
Lay in the spinach, let it simmer for 10 minutes.
Break 5 or 6 eggs, each one separately in a cup, then put the eggs on the spinach.
When all the eggs are in, sprinkle over some pepper and salt, let them boil with the spinach.
When they are set dish them up gently, not to disturb the eggs.

title: Befsztyk (Beefsteak)
description: Prepared with meat, butter or fat, and salt.
steps: The best beefsteak is fried on an iron grill over which fire burns and flame reaches almost the meat
If such a grill is not available, fry on a skillet on very high heat
Commonly used in America are the following cuts: tenderloin, porterhouse, short porterhouse, and sirloin; porterhouse is considered the best
A good beefsteak must be cut one inch thick, and generally the larger the slice, the better the beefsteak

Since the quality of beefsteak depends largely on high heat during frying, when frying on a skillet it is probably best to use fat rather than butter, as the temperature of hot fat is higher than butter, but after frying on fat, smear the beefsteak with butter
It is important that the meat not be beaten or salted at all—salt it only after frying
Always fry the entire slice of meat, never cut it into pieces
Serve only with the meat juice remaining on the skillet
Fry briefly, at most ten to fifteen minutes, and after frying the meat should be red inside
Immediately after frying, smear the beefsteak with butter and serve
Serve with potatoes as a vegetable, preferably fried French style

Add one packet of yeast dissolved in milk and add more milk so the batter is thin.
Place in a warm location.
When it rises too much, stir it and repeat this mixing each time the batter rises too much.
It is best to prepare the batter in the morning so it is ready to use in a few hours.
Ten minutes before frying the pancakes, beat in four egg yolks.
Beat the whites into a foam and also add to the batter, mixing gently.
Fry on a small pan, pouring the batter with a spoon so it spreads over the whole pan.
When browned on one side, flip with a spatula or knife to the other side.
After frying, stack one on top of another on a platter which should stand on the stove or over steam.
Grease the pan with clarified butter.
Serve these pancakes with melted butter and sour cream.

steps: After cleaning the turkey, discard the giblets and carefully butterfly it along the backbone, remove the bones, cut away meat remaining on the bones

Season with salt and spread a layer of the following filling on the flattened turkey: Take one pound of young pork fat, cut into pieces and sauté without browning; take one pound of veal, veal liver and turkey liver, braise all in the fat, then pass through a meat grinder, then strain through a sieve, add salt and pepper to taste, a pinch of nutmeg, two soaked and squeezed bread rolls and three eggs; mix everything properly and spread a one-inch thick layer on the flattened turkey

Over this spread a layer of slices of young cooked pork fat alternating with meat cut from the turkey and strips of ham or tongue, then again a layer of filling; if desired, add several olives to the filling
Roll the prepared turkey carefully, sew it shut, wrap in a napkin, shaping it into an oblong form, tie with twine and cook in salted water with mixed vegetables and four calf's feet for three hours

After cooking, remove from heat and let rest for one hour, then remove the turkey, unwrap the napkin and rinse in clean hot water, soak in cold water, wrap in the napkin again and press down with a weight so all sauce drains

From the remaining sauce, remove all fat, clarify with two egg whites beaten with water, remove from heat, add juice of half a lemon, then strain through a napkin, and place in a cold place to set as aspic
When the turkey has completely cooled, slice it, arrange on a platter and coat with aspic
Galantine can be made in the same way with chicken

steps: Take plums not overly ripe, sort them, pour into a pot, place on the fire and crush the plums so as to extract all the juice from them
Pour all the mass into a bag and press out the juice, then strain it several more times so that it is clear
For one pound of juice obtained this way, add one pound of sugar, or less if the plums are sweet
First place the sugar in the oven and heat it well, being careful not to burn it
Pour the pressed juice back into the pot and boil for about twenty minutes, then add the hot sugar and stir until it dissolves completely
Pour into jars or glasses and place in the sun until the jelly sets
